problem: VLN agents show a large performance drop from seen to unseen environments (environment bias), but this gap was only noted as a challenge and never explained or diagnosed.
motivation: Generalization to unseen environments is the core goal of instruction-guided navigation, so understanding where and why the bias arises matters. The authors run diagnostic experiments, excluding language and navigation graph and re-splitting environments, to find that low-level ResNet visual appearance is the culprit.
key_idea: Environment bias in VLN stems from low-level visual appearance in ResNet features, so replacing them with higher-level semantic features (detection areas, semantic segmentation) shrinks the seen-unseen gap without changing the agent or its training.
insight: Language distance analysis and a vision-masked agent (38.5 seen / 41.0 unseen, 2.5 gap) rule out instructions and the graph as the cause. Re-splitting shows path-level, region-level and environment-level localities. Replacing ResNet with ImageNet probabilities nearly closes the gap (R2R 1.1, R4R 0.2), and semantic segmentation features also raise unseen SR (R2R GT-Seg 56.2 vs 47.5), suggesting environments/regions have their own visual styles that ResNet features overfit to.
method: Diagnosis of language: ROUGE-L/BLEU-4 distance between val and training instructions shows seen still beats unseen at equal distance, so language is not the cause
Diagnosis of graph: zero out ResNet features so the agent uses only instruction and graph; the seen-unseen gap is only 2.5 points

Structural re-splitting: X-split and Z-split of training houses create path-seen, path-unseen, and env-unseen validation sets, revealing path-, region- and environment-level localities (region level measured by max-min graph distance to training viewpoints)
ImageNet-label features: frozen 1000-way ResNet classifier probabilities replace the 2048-d mean-pooled features
Detection features: Faster R-CNN (Visual Genome, Bottom-Up) confidence-weighted object areas per class, 152-d

Semantic segmentation features: 42-d class-area vectors from Matterport3D GT segmentation (GT-Seg), or predicted from ResNet by a 3-layer MLP (2048-512-256-42, BCE loss, trained on 51 of 61 training envs, 10 for validation) (Learned-Seg)
Baseline agent: panoramic Follower (Fried et al.) with EnvDrop modifications, trained with imitation learning only, no RL or augmentation

setting.backbone: Follower attentive encoder-decoder with EnvDrop modifications (trained from scratch, imitation learning); ResNet-152, Faster R-CNN, and a small MLP as feature extractors
setting.training_data: R2R, R4R, CVDN training splits (imitation learning only); Learned-Seg MLP trained on GT semantic areas of 51 training environments
setting.observation: panoramic views as ResNet / ImageNet-probability / detection-area / semantic-segmentation-area features
setting.simulator: Matterport3D simulator (Touchdown for the outdoor gap analysis)
setting.privileged: GT-Seg variant uses ground-truth Matterport3D semantic segmentation at test time; Learned-Seg and other variants use none

numbers.evidence: Table 1/3: Learned-Seg R2R Val Seen 52.6, Val Unseen 53.3, gap 0.7

numbers.backbone: Follower baseline + GT semantic segmentation features
numbers.extra: uses ground-truth semantic segmentation of test environments

numbers.backbone: Follower baseline + GT semantic segmentation features

numbers_note: Success rates are R2R/R4R validation SR under greedy decoding; only SR (or GP for CVDN) reported, no SPL/NE. Touchdown re-split results also reported (baseline 17.5 vs 5.3) but omitted since it is not an own-method variant.
results: Semantic features greatly shrink the seen-unseen gap: R2R gap goes from 8.6 (ResNet) to 0.7 (Learned-Seg), R4R from 23.9 to 3.7, and CVDN from 3.55 to 1.41. Unseen performance also rises (R2R 47.5→53.3 Learned-Seg, 56.2 GT-Seg), and the features generalize to SMNA (38.0→40.6) and Regretful (42.7→47.3).
limitations: Only the low-level ResNet appearance explanation is tested; with semantic features, performance is bounded by semantic quality (ImageNet features lower unseen results in R4R)
GT-Seg requires ground-truth segmentation of test environments, and Learned-Seg gives up seen accuracy (R2R 56.1→52.6)
Baselines trained with imitation learning only, no RL or augmentation, so results are not directly comparable to top SOTA systems
